title: Bourbon Street in the 1930s and John Handy
summary: Playing at Sam Colombo's on Bourbon Street, sidemen, and a discussion of John Handy on saxophone and clarinet.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Yeah, well I played on Bourbon Street in the 30s at 802 for Sam Columbo. It was right across from the paddock. When the paddock was open up, I had been out there playing across the street. Little Sammy Hopkins was on the piano. Charlie, what's his name? Charlie Sylvester was playing the drum. And Chester Lazard was playing the bass. And then later on we got Handy out there. I played there a long time for him. Who's Handy? John Handy, the saxophone player.
Could be other Handys too, you know. There's a many. I'm sorry, I'm sorry.
That's okay. I just said it the way I can, you should know what I'm talking about. I do know. John Handy, yeah.
I want those boys in England to know. Yeah that's right, John Handy. So he was playing saxophone. He was playing saxophone. That's right. Did you ever work with him on clarinet?

Well, no, the time when he was playing a lot of clarinet, he was the best you had here. He was working at the Humminbird on Biennale and Marie, and I was playing at a nightclub on Iberville between Marie and Villery. And like I said, most of my work at that time was of my own.
I was the leader of my band. Well what kind of clarinet was he playing then, would you call it? Was he reading or faking or what?
He was faking. He was faking, but he was great.
Did he play a lot of notes or what?
Well I wouldn't be able to explain exactly how I went, but he was really good.
Yeah, you know he's made some records, I don't know if you've ever heard of him.
No, I went over by George to listen one day and George happened not to be there. I had a chance to hear the records. With Punch I think it was.
Yeah. Tom or somebody. Punch. Yeah. I could play some tapes of him, but I'd better not. I think his lip was down when he made those records.

I'll tell you about him, he just lost interest in it. He don't like to play. That's for sure. Because when I was on Bourbon Street after some time back I had my own band at the Mardi Gras for quite a while out there for Sid. And then I played on Tuesdays with the band and I got him out there and he said it was all right until he gets on the stand and he found all kind of fault. He just don't like to play it.
Well there's very few guys who can play both alto and clarinet I notice. Well I don't know. Not too many of them can do it. I know it don't seem to bother Contrell.
He played a tenor in that. Yeah but alto I say in clarinet.
Maybe it's a change of key or something you know. I don't know. It seems to get him.
He just after he played so much saxophone he just played.
